source: Twenty-seven US states specifically target clinics that provide abortions with laws called “Targeted Regulation of Abortion Providers,” also known as TRAP laws.
why: External count of state laws; cities.csv contains city driving times and populations only, with no TRAP-law or state-policy data.

source: In 2013, Texas passed a TRAP law called House Bill 2 (HB2). Out of the 41 clinics open in Texas at the time, only five fully met the new requirements.
why: External clinic-compliance counts from the HB2 period; cities.csv has no clinic-level records or compliance status.

source: As the number of operating clinics in Texas was cut in half
why: External historical count of Texas clinics; cities.csv has no clinic-opening or clinic-closing records.

source: when nearby clinics close, pregnant patients experience an “undue burden” to travel upward of 150 miles to the nearest clinic.
why: The 150-mile distance comes from the court case and is not in cities.csv, which reports round-trip driving hours rather than miles.

source: This drive would take about 5 hours round trip
why: This is derived from the external 150-mile distance at 75 miles per hour, not from the driving-time columns in cities.csv.

source: it could have impacted the nearly 275,000 women of reproductive age living in Texas’ Rio Grande Valley.
why: External population estimate for the Rio Grande Valley; cities.csv has city populations but no age breakdown or Rio Grande Valley aggregate.

source: Although 89% of abortions occur when the patient is less than 12 weeks pregnant
why: External Guttmacher statistic; cities.csv has no abortion-incidence data by gestational age.

source: This same pattern of decreased access to abortion-providing clinics can be found in both rural and urban areas across the country.
why: cities.csv contains only cities with population greater than 50,000 (the story's urban-area definition) and has no rural locations or rural/urban classification, so the claimed rural-and-urban pattern cannot be computed.

source: Utah requires that patients are present for two appointments spaced three days apart before abortion services can be provided.
why: External state-law detail; cities.csv has no appointment, waiting-period or regulatory data.

source: In the first half of 2017, six states proposed TRAP laws to ban abortion entirely, and 28 states have proposed laws to ban abortion under some circumstances. Clinics in these 34 states are potentially in danger of drastic closures
why: External legislative counts; cities.csv has no bill, state-policy or clinic-risk data.

source: Data for this story excluded hospitals and physicians because clinics account for about 95% of annual abortions in the US.
why: External share of annual abortions; cities.csv has no hospital, physician or abortion-count records.
